The outbreak coincides with rising dengue and typhoid activity in Manipur, with other skin, fungal, and bacterial infections also reported. When symptoms occur, they typically include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle pains, nausea/vomiting, skin rashes, and swollen lymph nodes; symptoms are usually mild and self-limited. When present, common signs include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle pains, nausea, vomiting, skin rashes, and swollen lymph nodes. Most cases are mild and resolve spontaneously, but a minority can involve the nervous system, causing meningitis, encephalitis, or meningoencephalitis, with confusion, seizures, tremors, muscle weakness, or paralysis. - As of 28 August 2026, Brazil reports four confirmed West Nile fever cases — two in São Paulo and two in Santa Catarina — with one fatality: a 77-year-old woman. A fifth case in Piauí is being investigated and not yet confirmed. West Nile fever is asymptomatic in about 50–80% of infections; when symptomatic it can cause fever, nausea, vomiting, and muscle pain, and about 1 in 150 individuals may develop severe neurological disease such as meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis. Severe cases may require ICU admission, intubation, and mechanical ventilation. There is no vaccine or specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive. Transmission involves birds transmitting the virus to mosquitoes, which then pass it to humans. The main risk areas are rural and wild settings.

article.articleHeadline: M18-China Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus GP38 Protein Shows Broad
article.articleSummary: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is geographically widespread across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and southeastern Europe. For diagnostics and vaccines, GP38 could enable broader cross-strain recognition, though cross-reactivity poses challenges.

Vall Companys pursues Latin America expansion (10% stake in Mexican Importadora Serrana; deals with Coexca Chile and Grupo Pacuca Argentina; 12 million loan). Additional measures: 61 million provision; dividend cut to 36 million; capex from 190 to 85 million.

article.articleHeadline: 39-year-old man contracts monkeypox after high-risk contact with two strangers during the incubation period.
article.articleSummary: A 39-year-old man in Hong Kong contracted monkeypox and, on Aug 29, 2026, was transferred to Princess Margaret Hospital for isolation with a stable condition. He developed fever and cervical lymphadenopathy on Aug 24, followed by oral ulcers and a rash affecting the face, trunk, limbs and genitals. He had high-risk contact with two unidentified men during the incubation period and had not received monkeypox vaccination. He visited Queen Elizabeth Hospital for a follow-up on Aug 26 and was subsequently admitted. Public Health Laboratory Service confirmed the infection. An epidemiological investigation is ongoing, with efforts to contact others who may have had high-risk exposure; the Centre for Health Protection will report the case to the World Health Organization. Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 97 monkeypox cases (77 local, 20 imported), all male, with most linked to high-risk sexual activity.

triage.headline_ja: 39歳男性、潜伏期間中に見知らぬ2人と高リスク接触後にサル痘（Mpox）に感染
triage.triage_reason: 香港での単発Mpox症例であり、2022年以降97例目の継続的な流行の一部。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、性的接触による感染拡大の可能性があり経過観察が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 'Behind every case, a person': the man leading DRC's Ebola fight on the human cost hidden behind the numbers
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo variant Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has 5,656 confirmed cases and 2,715 deaths as of 24 August, the largest and deadliest outbreak since 1976 and the 17th in the DRC; outbreak first declared in May. Prof. Pierre Akilimali, head of the National Public Health Institute and incident manager for a multi-agency response, emphasizes that behind every case is a person and a family, while acknowledging cases may rise as community engagement improves and treatment centres adapt. Cross-border risk involves Uganda, which has recently declared itself Ebola-free after several border cases. The eastern DRC’s war-weary, distrustful context includes attacks on clinics, complicating response. The effort calls for regional and international solidarity, with concerns about funds channeled through NGOs and delayed wages; authorities insist responses must strengthen, not collapse, the broader health system and maintain access to care for other conditions.

triage.headline_ja: 『すべての症例の背後に一人の人間がいる』：数字の裏に隠されたコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ対応を率いる男が語る人的犠牲
triage.triage_reason: DRCで1976年以来最大・最悪規模のエボラ流行（確定5,656例、死亡2,715例）が継続中であり、越境リスクや医療体制崩壊の懸念があるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダは越境リスクとして言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ウガンダ自体はエボラ終息を宣言済み。

article.articleHeadline: Monkeypox (mpox) is spreading again: The virus has appeared in new countries. Can the outbreak be stopped?
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) is resurfacing globally, with Guinea-Bissau reporting its first cases, signaling spread to new countries. Since 2022, nearly 190,000 lab-confirmed mpox infections have been reported in 145 countries. The illness begins with flu-like symptoms (fever, chills, muscle pains) and then a vesicular rash that crusts. Mpox is endemic in parts of Africa and has spread beyond, driven by two clades: Congo Basin (Clade I) and West African (Clade II); West African spurred the 2022 outbreak, while a newer Clade I was detected in DR Congo in 2024. The WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern in Aug 2024 and lifted it in Sept 2025 as cases declined. UNICEF reports 46 suspected cases in Guinea-Bissau, including 23 children under 15, with higher risk for severe disease in young children. Vaccines exist for exposed or high-risk individuals, but supplies remain concentrated in high-income countries.

triage.headline_ja: サル痘（Mpox）が再び拡大：ウイルスが新たな国々で確認される。流行は食い止められるか？
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準が複数該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な拡大、国際的拡大リスク）し、WHOが過去にPHEICを宣言した経緯もあることからフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は主にギニアビサウでの初症例報告（対象国リスト外）だが、DRCでのClade I検出（2024年）についても言及されており、既知の流行状況として対象国に含めた。ギニアビサウは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: The viruses that defined the first half of 2026: from Bundibugyo ebolavirus to the resurgence of measles.
article.articleSummary: First half of 2026 features multiple infectious disease threats, led by a Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ituri province with cross-border spread to Uganda; the WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17 and Africa CDC issued a continental emergency. No licensed vaccine or approved specific therapy exists for Bundibugyo; response relies on classic public health measures while trialing antivirals MBP134 (monoclonal antibody) and remdesivir in collaboration with Oxford. Europe maintains very low overall risk but remains vigilant for imported cases and strengthens border and health-system readiness. Measles resurgence continues globally (Europe, Africa, Asia) due to declines in vaccination and uneven recovery post-pandemic, underscoring the goal of restoring vaccination coverages above 95%. Nipah remains a priority with high fatality potential, bats of genus Pteropus as reservoirs; no vaccines or treatments; ongoing surveillance. Hantavirus episodes trigger attention to zoonoses.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年上半期を特徴づけたウイルス：ブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスから麻疹の再流行まで
triage.triage_reason: DRCイツリ州で発生したブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスのアウトブレイクに対しWHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言し、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準を複数満たすシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 本記事は2026年上半期の複数感染症（エボラ、麻疹、ニパ、ハンタウイルス）を総括するレビュー記事だが、DRCのブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスアウトブレイクはWHO PHEIC宣言・Africa CDC大陸緊急事態宣言を伴う重大イベントであるため主題として抽出。ウガンダ・英国・アフリカ大陸は対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。麻疹・ニパ・ハンタウイルスは地域特定が不明確なため個別評価対象外とした。

article.articleHeadline: Rare Ebola Case Shows 10-Fold Higher Throat Viral RNA
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus infection in a 39-year-old American healthcare worker, acquired in Ituri Province, DRC. On day 5, throat RNA was over tenfold higher than plasma RNA, an unusual distribution versus typical Ebola patterns. Three laboratories failed to culture replication-capable virus from throat, plasma or semen; RNA detection does not prove infectious virus. There is no Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or approved therapy; rVSV-ZEBOV given ~41 months earlier is unlikely protective. He received MBP134 monoclonal antibodies (50 mg/kg) under FDA IND and an off-label remdesivir (200 mg loading). He arrived in Berlin on day 5 and was treated in isolation; RNA declined and was undetectable by day 13 in tested samples, though semen remained positive on day 20 (~2,500 copies/mL) and negative by day 25. He was discharged on day 22. The case highlights diagnostic limits and exposure risks for healthcare workers; a cluster of hemorrhagic deaths was reported in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: まれなエボラ症例、咽頭ウイルスRNAが血漿の10倍高値を示す
triage.triage_reason: DRCイトゥリ州で発生したブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス感染例において、通常と異なるウイルス学的分布が確認され、精液からもRNAが検出された。加えて同地域で出血熱による死亡クラスターが報告されており、国際搬送も発生していることからIHR基準複数該当と判断。
triage.notes: 本症例はDRCイトゥリ州で感染し国際搬送・治療された個別の医学症例報告だが、記事末尾で同地域における出血熱死亡クラスターの発生が言及されており、公衆衛生上のアウトブレイク文脈が存在する可能性がある。ベルリンでの治療は発生地域ではなく搬送先であるため verified_locations から除外した。続報でクラスターの詳細（規模・死亡率・地域拡大）を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: The Ebola outbreak: 'a perfect storm'
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surpassed 2,500 deaths after more than 100 days, with a mortality rate near 50% and children accounting for about one-third of fatalities. The Bundibugjo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment, though clinical trials are underway. The outbreak has spread to six provinces, concentrated in Ituri province in north-eastern Congo where ongoing conflict and militias persist, and more than 900,000 people have been displaced as gold mining draws workers from wide areas. Fears exist that the virus could reach South Sudan and Kinshasa. The response is struggling to keep pace, worsened by cuts to Western aid, including USAID dismantling and the withdrawal from the World Health Organization, undermining health infrastructure and surveillance. Described as a "perfect storm" of factors hindering containment.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in the DRC: the British scientific adviser evaluates it.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak persists in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with focus on Ituri and Kinshasa as UK Chief Scientific Adviser Professor John Edmunds completes a four-day mission (Aug 27, 2026) to assess the response. London has mobilized nearly $29 million to support emergency operations, field logistics, and direct technical assistance, including vaccine development and deployment. Edmunds, speaking with Radio Okapi, discussed on-the-ground effectiveness of control measures, remaining needs, and ongoing UK support to Congolese teams; he outlined prospects for intensified UK–Kinshasa cooperation. The mission comes amid security challenges hindering health operations. The outbreak remains active in the region, with continued funding and strategic guidance from the UK to back the response.

article.articleHeadline: Kindu: nearly 100 cases of chickenpox, with no deaths reported at the central prison (official).
article.articleSummary: Chickenpox (varicella) outbreak at Kindu central prison, Maniema, with 97 cases reported since the outbreak began in week 20; by week 35, no deaths had been recorded. An investigation led by Faustin Bikonda, head of the Maniema Provincial Health Division, visited the prison on August 27, 2026. Infected inmates showed skin eruptions, suggesting varicella rather than measles; samples were taken and some patients received medications from the Kindu health zone. Authorities urged the isolation of sick inmates to limit transmission, a priority given the facility’s severe overcrowding (built for about 250 inmates but housing 644). The strategy emphasizes separating uninfected individuals from the ill and treating those who are sick. Despite multiple meetings with provincial and prison authorities, isolation had not yet been implemented during the visit, and drug stock shortages were noted, with calls to strengthen infection prevention measures.

article.articleHeadline: Dolly Parton's Health Struggles; Fauci Prosecution Stalled; Germany's Malaria Deaths
article.articleSummary: Two workers at Germany's Frankfurt Airport died after contracting malaria believed to have been carried into the country by an air passenger, underscoring imported malaria risk in Europe. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, authorities began vaccinating health workers and other frontline responders as part of the ongoing Ebola outbreak response, signaling continued international public health efforts. In Norway, King Harald V died at 89 following hospitalization for a bacterial infection of the blood, a case highlighting sepsis-related mortality in high-income nations. The report also notes tirzepatide (Mounjaro) receiving an expanded indication to lower cardiovascular risk in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes, reflecting ongoing advances in diabetes management.

article.articleHeadline: Butembo: four health centers burned in a month amid rumors about Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Four health facilities in Butembo, North Kivu, have been set ablaze within a month amid Ebola-related rumors. The latest is the Bethesda dispensary in Vuromo-Kakuva (Mukuna, Katwa health zone), burned in the early hours of August 27 by unidentified perpetrators; rumors claim patients died there. Earlier, on August 18, Bora Maisha Hospital in Mukalangirwa was torched following a confirmed Ebola case, according to a health source. Previously, on July 29, two facilities—Crinovic Hospital in Kavikene (Congo ya Sika, Vulamba) and the Zawadi health post (Mapendo) in Kyaghala (Bulengera)—were attacked within 48 hours, amid threats against health workers and suspicions of collusion with Ebola response efforts. The incidents reflect a climate of fear and rumor around Ebola in Butembo, with authorities yet to identify perpetrators and to clarify the outbreak status from this report.

triage.headline_ja: ブテンボ:エボラを巡る噂を背景に1か月で4つの保健センターが放火される
triage.triage_reason: エボラ関連の噂により医療施設への放火が相次いでおり、確認済み症例の存在や公衆衛生対応の妨害が示唆されるため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラの感染状況そのものよりも、噂による医療施設への暴力・放火事件を主題としている。確認済み症例(confirmed Ebola case)への言及があるが、現在の疫学的状況（症例数、死亡数等）は不明。医療対応妨害が続発症例把握や対策実施の障害となり得るため注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is not just a medical crisis - it is also one of trust
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo: more than 100 days after declaration, the disease has claimed over 2,500 lives across the DRC, with 900 Red Cross volunteers serving and reaching more than 100,000 people. Misinformation and fear erode trust, reducing help-seeking, reporting, and acceptance of safe and dignified burials. Twelve colleagues were injured, and three died in May before the outbreak was identified, highlighting risks to responders. Practical changes include using body bags with clear material over the faces of loved ones to let families see them during mourning. Lessons from the 2018 outbreak—door-to-door information and radio outreach—are guiding current efforts. Reduced aid funding further weakens response and trust. The article emphasizes that trust must be built within communities, and that governments, tech platforms, and humanitarian actors must work with communities to counter misinformation and save lives.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクは医療危機だけでなく、信頼の危機でもある
triage.triage_reason: 宣言から100日以上が経過し死者2500人超に達する大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであり、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo: Ituri - MONUSCO deploys a mobile base of operations at Niania to secure the Ebola response.
article.articleSummary: MONUSCO deployed a mobile base in Niania, Mambasa territory, Ituri, to reinforce security for the Ebola response in the area about 350 km southwest of Bunia. Installed for a week by Bangladeshi peacekeepers, the base secures Ebola treatment centers, health workers, and humanitarian teams amid security challenges, including attacks on the PK51 treatment center attributed to locals. Niania's health area has over 200 confirmed Ebola cases and 123 deaths. The MONUSCO force also conducts joint patrols and escorts convoys, supporting FARDC. A Bangladeshi contingent is already operating in Mongwalu, Djugu, for three months, with officials urging stronger collaboration to access exposed zones. In addition to outbreak response, the peacekeepers help protect civilians from armed groups, notably the ADF.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：イツリ州 - MONUSCOがニアニアにエボラ対応支援のための機動展開基地を設置
triage.triage_reason: イツリ州ニアニア保健地域で200例以上の確定エボラ症例・123名の死亡が報告されており、治安上の問題（治療センターへの攻撃）で対応が妨げられている深刻な進行中のアウトブレイクである。
triage.notes: MaliのKoulikoro地域が発生地域に含まれているが、記事本文はDRCのエボラアウトブレイク（イツリ州）に関するものであり、Maliは対象国外かつ主題ではないため除外した。国連平和維持軍(MONUSCO)がエボラ対応支援と治安維持の両方に従事しており、武装勢力(ADF)による攻撃が対応を妨げている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: The Kinshasa Basketball Camp 2026 postponed due to Ebola [Press Release].
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa Basketball Camp 2026 has been postponed due to an Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The event, scheduled for August 24–30, 2026 at Kinshasa’s Stade des Jeux de la Francophonie, was deferred after evolving health conditions and authorities’ recommendations, in consultation with all stakeholders. The camp would have brought together about 500 youths from 26 provinces, 50 coaches, and 20–30 NBA/WNBA stars, with more than 10,000 spectators. Given that most beneficiaries are minors, organizers opted for maximum caution. The decision was announced by Didier MBENGA, Ambassador of Sports of the DRC, under the patronage of President Félix Tshisekedi. New dates will be announced after official end of the epidemic; reprogramming is envisaged for the first half of 2027, subject to validation. Participants, families, leagues, and partners will be informed individually; authorities urge adherence to prevention measures and rejection of rumors.

triage.headline_ja: キンシャサ・バスケットボールキャンプ2026、エボラ出血熱のため延期【プレスリリース】
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラウイルス病流行により大統領後援の国際的スポーツイベントが延期されるなど、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と社会的関心の高さが確認されるため。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: the DRC and Uganda commit to strengthening cross-border cooperation - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda pledged to strengthen cross-border cooperation to curb Ebola transmission, after a meeting in Hoima, Uganda, on 28 August 2026. Jean Nsiro, the military administrator of Irumu territory in northeast DRC, said the talks aimed to formalize cross-border movements and tighten border controls to reduce transmission risk. He stressed that delaying formalization increases outbreak risks and pointed to clandestine, especially nocturnal, crossings that heighten health threats. Participants sought to establish a joint plan with concrete on-the-ground actions, noting that progress is hampered by remaining obstacles. The overarching goal is to stop transmission of the Ebola epidemic through officialized, supervised cross-border movement and coordinated public health measures between the two neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダ、国境を越えた協力強化を約束
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国北東部（イルム準州）でのエボラ流行が継続しており、ウガンダとの国境を越えた感染拡大リスクが指摘されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国イルム準州（北東部）で継続中のエボラ流行と、ウガンダとの国境管理・越境協力強化に関する会合について述べている。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、越境感染リスクとして言及されている点は重要。夜間の密航的な越境が感染拡大要因として指摘されており、地域的な公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Bunia: Compliance with Sanitary Measures Required at Entry Points - ACP
article.articleSummary: Three entry-control points in Bunia—Mudzibala, Délé, and Tchaï—in Ituri, northeastern DRC, were emphasized to enforce sanitary measures amid an Ebola outbreak; a mission found resistance to guidelines among some travelers. Bunia currently records a high number of confirmed Ebola cases, with these points acting as potential routes for spread. Coordinator Jean-Claude Mukendi urged stronger community outreach and participation of administrative authorities, security services, health workers, and residents to curb transmission. Security teams are prepared to accompany health teams at checkpoints and to urge travelers to comply. The visit followed an incident at Mudzibala checkpoint in which a response worker was assaulted by youths. This underscores the need for reinforced sanitary practices at points of entry to limit contamination.

article.articleHeadline: Hunting Down the Last Cases of Sleeping Sickness
article.articleSummary: Sleeping sickness, or gambiense human African trypanosomiasis (gHAT), persists in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with a couple hundred cases still detected nationwide; 471 cases were reported worldwide in 2025, most in the DRC. EU-backed STROGHAT trials test a radically simpler strategy around acoziborole, a single-dose oral drug with 98.1% efficacy in clinical trials, to accelerate elimination. The approach uses mobile teams to screen villages; anyone with a positive test is treated—three tablets under supervision—while samples are sent for confirmatory lab testing. Historically, dangerous melarsoprol and lab-heavy, lumbar puncture–dependent protocols delayed treatment. Acoziborole is safer, avoiding hospitalization, and could simplify remote delivery. The strategy aims to stop transmission by 2030; since humans are the main reservoir, every infected person must be found and treated to prevent resurgence.

Reports serve as an early-detection system, enabling field teams to conduct inspections, diagnose, treat, quarantine, or vaccinate as needed. The service also educates farmers, collects data to map disease patterns, plan programs, and budget. It oversees livestock movement, slaughter, and veterinary drug distribution, and handles issues like fake feed or expired medicines. article.articleHeadline: HIV Cases in South Halmahera Regency Increase Each Year, Health Office Head Urges Vigilance Against Transmission
article.articleSummary: 210 confirmed HIV cases in South Halmahera Regency, North Maluku, Indonesia, as of 28 August 2026, per the Halmahera Selatan Health Office. The tally comprises 183 cases accumulated in 2024–2025 and 27 cases from January–July 2026. Health Office Head Asia Hasyim explains HIV damages immune cells and can progress to AIDS—typically about a decade after infection—leaving patients vulnerable to infections. Transmission occurs via contact with HIV-containing body fluids: blood, semen, vaginal fluids, anal fluids, and breast milk, with the highest incidence linked to sex with changing partners. Authorities urge vigilance to prevent transmission and warn of potential spread to adolescents; parents and couples should monitor activities. To improve early detection and management, the Halmahera Selatan Health Office will continue expanding the Free Health Check program (Cek Kesehatan Gratis, CKG).

article.articleSummary: Zika virus in Bali prompted the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to issue a Travel Health Notice on August 7, 2026, warning travelers returning from Bali about potential infection. The notice notes that Zika transmission predominantly occurs through Aedes mosquito bites and can also spread from pregnant women to their fetuses, as well as via sexual contact. While the article does not report a confirmed local outbreak or case counts, it cites infections among travelers who have returned from Bali. The warning highlights heightened risk for vulnerable groups, especially pregnant individuals, given the association between Zika infection during pregnancy and serious birth defects. Travelers planning trips to Bali or returning from Bali should take preventive measures against mosquito bites and practice safe sex to mitigate transmission.

Natuna authorities stress no local HFMD cases yet but maintain heightened surveillance due to substantial cross‑border mobility via ports and airports linking Batam to the rest of the Riau Islands. HFMD is described as a viral illness that typically resolves on its own and is not considered highly dangerous. Preventive guidance emphasizes personal hygiene and adherence to PHBS (Clean and Healthy Living Behavior). The article highlights vigilance at border communities to curb spread while Batam experiences ongoing transmission.

article.articleHeadline: In addition to the NTT earthquake victims, the Ministry of Health treats 35 residents infected with rabies in Nagekeo.
article.articleSummary: Earthquake of magnitude 7.7 struck Flores, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) on 15 August 2026. The Ministry of Health mobilized 392 health workers and deployed two inflatable field hospitals in Ruteng (Manggarai) and Mbay (Nagekeo). In the past week, 18 trauma patients were treated: 4 conservatively and 14 operated, including a complex multi-site fracture repair of the clavicle, forearm, and ankle in the inflatable facility. As of 26 August 2026, 105 people have died; 385 severely injured; 1,287 mildly injured; and more than 185,000 displaced across 444 evacuation sites. Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) dominates survivor complaints with 9,668 cases. Separately, 35 animal-bite rabies cases were recorded in Nagekeo, all receiving complete vaccination. The ministry maintains medical logistics and referrals, relocating services if facilities are damaged to ensure patient and staff safety.

article.articleHeadline: Few chikungunya cases in Yogyakarta, Indonesia: emerging public health
article.articleSummary: Four chikungunya infections were detected among 7,600 dengue-negative patients in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, within a cross-sectional 8,000 febrile cases; 400 dengue-PCR-positive results were also identified. RT-PCR confirms current infection but detects virus only during a short viraemic window, so a single sampling may underestimate total infections. Researchers are testing a random subset of the 8,000 samples serologically to estimate past exposure and protective immunity, which could indicate hidden immunity or a largely susceptible population. Bali remains a recognized chikungunya hotspot (2021–2022 incidence ~20.6/100,000). Java’s dense population and movement could sustain transmission; North and South Sulawesi reported >50% chikungunya IgG in some cohorts, while Ambon, Banjarmasin and Batam show low hospital-detected rates. Indonesia’s annual case counts fluctuated: 2,974 (2022), 6,049 (2023), 571 (2024). Vaccines IXCHIQ and Vimkunya have licensure and are moving toward public-health use.

article.articleHeadline: Baubau Health Office trains Puskesmas program managers to tackle leprosy and frambesia.
article.articleSummary: Baubau City Health Office in Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, trains puskesmas program managers to accelerate tackling leprosy and frambusia in Baubau and surrounding areas. The training, organized with Balai Pelatihan Kesehatan (Bapelkes) of Southeast Sulawesi, aims to align perceptions, boost competencies, and strengthen frontline capacity for early detection and case management. A comprehensive approach includes intensified health promotion, proactive case finding, proper treatment, and preventive medication to curb transmission. Emphasis on early detection reflects that delayed diagnosis of leprosy can cause permanent disability. Health workers are urged to be vigilant for skin lesions and conduct active field surveillance. Participants will implement a digital reporting system to ensure accurate data for policy decisions, and cascade knowledge to doctors, nurses, and midwives across the network. This supports ongoing elimination of leprosy and eradication of frambusia as of 28 August 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Baubau City Government trains laboratory personnel to strengthen malaria detection.
article.articleSummary: Baubau City, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, is strengthening malaria detection by training Medical Laboratory Technologists (ATLM) to maintain its malaria-elimination status. The refresher malaria microscopy training, conducted with the Sulawesi Tenggara Health Training Center (Bapelkes Sultra), aims to sustain early detection and prevent re-emergence, as elimination remains at risk. National malaria cases rose from 543,965 in 2024 to 706,297 in 2025, while Baubau is among 401 Indonesian districts/cities that have kept malaria elimination. To prevent re-emergence, Baubau requires all clinically suspected malaria cases in health facilities to undergo laboratory confirmation via microscopy or Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT). Yuslina, head of Prevention and Control of Diseases, emphasizes that lab-confirmed results safeguard against inappropriate treatment and potential antimalarial resistance. Ongoing capacity strengthening is deemed vital to ensure rapid and accurate case finding across facilities.

article.articleHeadline: 71 Rabies-Positive Cases in Jembrana, Bali; Vaccination Target Pursued, 76 Percent Achieved.
article.articleSummary: Rabies-positive animal cases in Jembrana district, Bali reached 71 in August 2026, with 7 new cases that month. Despite the rising month, authorities say the overall figures are still below 2025, which recorded 116 positive rabies cases in animals. Vaccination campaigns and population control, including sterilization and vaccination of rabies-transmitting animals (HPR), are being intensified. On August 28, 2026, sterilization and vaccination activities were conducted at Gedung Pendopo Kesari, Negara District. As of August 2026, vaccination coverage stands at 76% of an estimated 40,400 animals, surpassing last year's 72% but short of the 90% target for the year to achieve herd immunity and reduce rabies spread. I Gusti Ngurah Putu Sugiarta, head of PKH, Dinas Pertanian, Perikanan dan Pangan Jembrana, emphasized prevention through vaccination and population control, including dogs, cats, and even macaques.

article.articleHeadline: Healthcare workers accompany the care of a patient with drug-resistant TB at Baznas Hospital
article.articleSummary: As of 29 August 2026, a patient with drug-resistant tuberculosis is being cared for at the Baznas Sahabat Paru Health House in Tangerang. Health personnel from local primary care centers provide alternating 14-day accompaniment to ensure regimen adherence, with medical staff and cadres supporting the patient. The facility—resulting from a Baznas and Tangerang City Health Office collaboration—has three rooms, each housing up to two patients, serving as temporary housing for stable drug-resistant TB cases. Patients are referred from RSUD Kota Tangerang and RS Sitanala, among other TB referral centers, for two weeks of treatment and specialist oversight, including pulmonologists. Baznas funds the program while Dinas Kesehatan handles beneficiary recruitment and medication adherence support.

article.articleHeadline: BKHIT Maluku Strengthens the Competencies of Laboratory Technicians for the Detection of Animal Diseases.
article.articleSummary: As of 29 August 2026, Ambon, Maluku Province, Indonesia, Balai Karantina Hewan, Ikan, dan Tumbuhan (BKHIT) Maluku strengthens laboratory competencies for rapid, accurate detection of animal and fish diseases via Real Time PCR (RT-PCR). article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases fall from 88.4 thousand to under 6 thousand in one year.
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases in Paraná, Brazil, dropped dramatically—from 88,488 cases in Aug 2025 to 5,878 confirmed by Aug 18, 2026, with five deaths this year (five in 2026 vs 129 by the same date in 2025). The 2025 epidemiological year totaled 305,594 notifications, 92,620 confirmed cases and 145 deaths; 2025 was the first year counted Jan–Dec, instead of mid-year to mid-year. In 2026, 4,890 autochthonous dengue cases have been confirmed in Paraná; remaining cases are imported. Despite the drop, El Niño-driven rains may increase Aedes aegypti breeding and transmission risk ahead of summer. Preventive measures include removing standing water, cleaning yards, and using repellent. A Wolbachia-release program continues to release infected mosquitoes to reduce vector development.

article.articleHeadline: Researchers from Roraima join project seeking new malaria drugs derived from the Brazil nut tree.
article.articleSummary: Malaria drug discovery in the Brazilian Amazon: Researchers from Roraima join a CNPEM Norte-Nordeste 2026 project to identify compounds from the Brazil nut tree (Bertholletia excelsa) that may inhibit Plasmodium proteins. The collaboration includes UFRR, Fiocruz Rondônia, Embrapa Rondônia, Fiocruz Amazônia, and UFAM, coordinated by Fernando Berton Zanchi, with CNPEM support and access to Sirius, Brazil’s particle accelerator. The study proceeds from computational screening to select promising molecules, followed by obtaining compounds and testing their ability to inhibit parasite proteins. Promising candidates will undergo detailed structural analysis via X-ray diffraction and synchrotron radiation. The initiative aims to yield new malaria drug candidates and expand knowledge of Amazonian biodiversity. Zazeri, CNPEM/Sirius ambassador in Roraima, highlights strengthened regional research networks and capacity-building for the Amazon.

article.articleHeadline: JJ: No vaccine rollout, Jundiaí records 469 dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: 469 confirmed dengue cases in Jundiaí, Brazil, in 2026, with Várzea Paulista at 94 and Itupeva at 5; Campo Limpo Paulista, Louveira, Cabreúva, and Jarinu did not report updated data but continue prevention efforts. The national rollout of the Butantan dengue vaccine remains suspended. In Jundiaí, vaccination for adults aged 59 and health workers has not resumed per the Ministry of Health; 8,831 dengue vaccine doses were administered in 2026, while adolescents aged 10–14 continue vaccination (13,816 first doses, 6,333 second doses). By comparison, 2025 saw 7,517 Jundiaí cases and 570 in Itupeva, while Várzea Paulista had 1,323 cases in 2025. The region’s dengue figures have fallen in 2026, reflecting ongoing Aedes aegypti control despite vaccine constraints.

article.articleHeadline: Upholding the Medical–Prevention Collaboration, Deepening International Cooperation — Academician Zhong Nanshan's Advice on Global Respiratory Disease Prevention and Control
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-28, at the Public Health and Management International Forum in Guangzhou, Academician Zhong Nanshan urged deeper medical prevention collaboration and international cooperation to curb global respiratory diseases, prioritizing Respiratory Syncytial Virus RSV. RSV is the leading cause of hospitalization for acute lower respiratory infections in infants and poses severe risk to the elderly and those with cardio-pulmonary conditions. Its burden remains under recognized by the public. The forum highlighted translating professional consensus into practical health actions, citing the earlier RSV Infection Prevention and Control Expert Consensus that promotes an integrated prevention–diagnosis–management framework and a shift from disease-centric to health-centric strategies. He warned that under 1 year olds are high risk; northern regions see winter-spring peaks, while the south has year-round transmission. A first RSV Awareness Month initiative and the Good Breathing program were launched. International cooperation via the Healthy Silk Road aims to share RSV/flu expertise with Portugal, Spain, Australia, Brazil, and Laos.

article.articleHeadline: How Deforestation in the Amazon Increases the Risk of Serious Diseases.
article.articleSummary: Field work in 2022 and 2024 in a rural settlement near Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil, links Amazon deforestation to higher risk of leishmaniasis and Chagas disease. Leishmaniasis risk rises as sandfly Nyssomyia antunesi establishes in landscapes with reduced forest cover, with vector abundance tied to the timing of deforestation and settlement stabilization. For Chagas, triatomine bugs infected with Trypanosoma cruzi occur on palms near homes; the shorter the distance between palm trees and houses, the more frequent the infected insects, increasing human exposure to the sylvatic cycle. Leishmaniasis is endemic in the Amazon and among WHO-listed neglected tropical diseases; Chagas poses fever and potential cardiac/digestive complications. Funded by FAPESP and Amazonia+10, the study aims to improve surveillance and to test area restoration with native species, involving local communities. Findings published in Parasites & Vectors and PLOS One.

article.articleHeadline: Lito Sousa wants to keep coming to Santa Catarina for an event even with a diagnosis of the rare disease Creutzfeldt-Jakob.
article.articleSummary: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) diagnosed in aviation expert Lito Sousa is not preventing his confirmed participation at the HJ Conference in Concórdia, western Santa Catarina, Brazil, scheduled for September 24–26, 2026; organizers will not use his image in campaigns but will keep him in the program if health permits. CJD is a rare, progressive prion neurodegenerative disease of the central nervous system, typically presenting with memory loss, cognitive decline, tremors, ataxia, behavioral changes, and rapid deterioration; most cases are sporadic. Diagnosis relies on MRI, EEG, CSF 14-3-3 protein testing, and PRNP genetic sequencing; definitive confirmation occurs post-mortem. Not contagious via casual contact. Forms include sporadic (~85%), hereditary (5–15%), and iatrogenic (<1%). In Brazil (2005–2021), 1,576 suspected cases were reported, with São Paulo, Paraná, and Minas Gerais leading; most patients aged 55–74, with a slight male predominance.

article.articleHeadline: Alagoas is at an alert level with severe cases of respiratory syndrome among children and adolescents, says Fiocruz.
article.articleSummary: Fiocruz's InfoGripe bulletin reports four capitals with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) activity at alert/risk/high risk in the last two weeks, with a rising long-term trend through week 33 (16–22 Aug). In Alagoas, increases are seen mainly among 2–14-year-olds; Mato Grosso and Roraima show upticks in 2–4-year-olds. Eight additional states—Amazonas, Mato Grosso do Sul, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, Santa Catarina, Sergipe—are at alert or higher but without long-term growth. Nationally, a mild rise in SARI among 2–14-year-olds is linked mainly to rhinovirus; reductions in <2s are attributed to RSV hospitalizations and influenza-related declines in other ages. RSV remains elevated in Roraima; influenza A season has ended; influenza B shows a small uptick in Bahia and Mato Grosso. COVID-19 incidence remains low. In 2026, 141,009 SARI cases with 76,126 positives (54%), 7,392 pending. Four capitals—Aracaju, Belém, Boa Vista, João Pessoa—show rising SARI activity.

article.articleHeadline: Death from diphtheria in Italy rekindles debate on vaccination and immunization in Brazil - BH 24 Horas
article.articleSummary: Diphtheria death in Italy of four-year-old Anna Rosa Bartolotta after her parents declined vaccination citing autism fears has revived the vaccination debate in Europe. A cousin began vaccination and is recovering; authorities are investigating the parents for involuntary homicide. Italy had no documented diphtheria cases for nearly three decades. The infection, caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae, can form toxic throat pseudomembranes and cause edema, lymphadenopathy, myocarditis, neuritis, or nephrotoxicity. Vaccination, part of the pentavalent schedule since 1923, is given at two months with boosters at four, six, and 15 months and at four years; adults require boosters every ten years. In Brazil, diphtheria is endemic but controlled, with only two cases in 2026 and five deaths since 2014. 2025 pentavalent-dose coverage was 89%, booster 87%, four-year vaccination 80%; tetanus-diphtheria vaccination in pregnant women about 82%, below the 95% goal. Health officials urge high coverage to prevent resurgence.

The technology aims to reduce the capacity of Aedes aegypti to transmit these diseases and to position the city as a regional hub for vector-control efforts. The announcement highlights a proactive approach to reducing arboviral transmission in the area, prioritizing a scalable intervention over traditional measures. No specific timelines, case counts, or laboratory-confirmation details are provided in the brief, but the plan underscores a long-term public health investment in the region.

article.articleHeadline: UK urged to ban imports of Brazilian meat over health concerns
article.articleSummary: UK farming bodies urge a ban on Brazilian meat over antimicrobial resistance concerns amid rising post-Brexit imports. NFU England warned public health is at risk from routine antibiotic use in Brazilian cattle and poultry and from non-compliance with EU rules. With the EU set to ban Brazilian beef and chicken week, the UK may not follow. UK imports from Brazil rose from about £3bn in 2021 to £5bn in 2025; 2024 Brazil accounted for about an eighth of UK chicken imports. Investigations by the Irish Farmers Journal/Association found easy access to antibiotics classified as highest-priority in human medicine without veterinary prescription and weak traceability. AMR is cited as causing around 1.14 million deaths annually and 4.71 million associated deaths. Defra says assessment of production systems is underway while monitoring EU ban impacts. A salmonella outbreak in imported eggs killed at least one person and sickened over 200 this month.

article.articleHeadline: Norovirus and intestinal bacteria send hundreds to the Azores' emergency departments.
article.articleSummary: Norovirus-driven acute gastroenteritis is affecting the Azores, with hundreds seeking care. By Aug 28, the Regional Health Authority (ARS) confirmed norovirus (GI and GII) on São Miguel and Faial. Isolated intestinal bacteria (Salmonella and Campylobacter) were detected in Ponta Delgada, São Miguel. The ARS reports a multi-island surge over several weeks, not a single-day outbreak. Faial had an early surge (>400 cases); transmission is now declining (Rt <1 since Aug 19). Flores and Terceira show declines after a late-August rebound; Corvo has no cases; Santa Maria, Graciosa and São Jorge lack data. Most cases present with vomiting and diarrhea and are mild; hospitalization is uncommon, with recovery at home in 1–3 days. Preventive actions include hand hygiene, 48-hour exclusion of symptomatic food handlers, and staying home 48 hours after symptoms end. Guidance via Linha Saúde Açores.

article.articleHeadline: Spotted fever spreads in Brazil; see symptoms, prevention, and when to seek medical care.
article.articleSummary: Spotted fever in Brazil, caused by Rickettsia and transmitted by star ticks, has 128 cases and 28 deaths. Symptoms after tick bite include severe headache, high fever, pains, local redness; severe cases may involve limb paralysis. In advanced disease, swelling and redness can appear on palms and soles, with diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and gangrene of ears or toes. Early diagnosis is challenging as symptoms mimic hepatitis, dengue, or leptospirosis; clinicians should consider exposure to tick habitats such as trails and farms. Prevention emphasizes reducing tick contact: light clothing, boots, long pants and sleeves, avoiding tall grass, and using repellents. If a tick is found, remove quickly with tweezers and wash the area; do not crush. Antibiotics started within two to three days are usually curative; a seven-day course may extend by three days after fever ends; delayed treatment increases risk of CNS, vascular, pulmonary, renal complications and death.

article.articleHeadline: Deaths of two sisters with similar symptoms put family and school on alert | São Gonçalo | O Dia
article.articleSummary: Two adolescent sisters, aged 16 (died July 29) and 14 (died Aug 22), died within 24 days in São Gonçalo, Rio de Janeiro, after presenting sore throat, fever, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain and dizziness. Two other children from the same family, aged 3 and 6, remain hospitalized with similar symptoms. No conclusive diagnosis or confirmed link between the deaths; investigations ongoing. A blood sample from the 14-year-old was sent to Lacen on July 24, with results expected within seven working days. The Colégio Estadual Augusto Cezário Diáz André (Pacheco) was sanitized on July 26; classes were briefly suspended. Vaccination of students at the school was planned for Aug 28 (municipal) or Aug 27 (state) as a preventive measure, not implying causation. Police report no record of a case; authorities continue to monitor and investigate.

article.articleHeadline: Alfenas suspends classes in daycares after human scabies cases | Rádio Itatiaia
article.articleSummary: Alfenas, Brazil suspended activities for seven days in two municipal daycare centers to curb a human scabies outbreak. The preventive measure began Aug 27, 2026. A total of 45 cases have been diagnosed across the two CEMEI facilities: 25 at CEMEI Professora Maria Conceição Carvalho - Dona Zinica (19 children, 6 adults) and 20 at CEMEI Dona Vanja (18 children, 2 adults). During the closure, buildings will undergo intensified cleaning and reorganization, while health teams conduct on-site assessments and refer those in need to local health posts. Authorities urge parents and guardians to seek medical evaluation if children present skin redness, lesions, or intense itching, especially at night. The guidance warns against self-treatment and stresses professional care for both children and staff at the units.

article.articleHeadline: Colombia records more than 70,000 dengue cases in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Colombia logged 70,350 dengue cases through the week ending 22 August 2026, per the National Institute of Health. About 60% had no warning signs and 1% progressed to severe dengue. National incidence is 210.8 per 100,000 at‑risk inhabitants; Meta, Amazonas, Guaviare, Magdalena, Casanare, Arauca and Bolívar report the highest rates (>530 per 100,000). Nationally, dengue notifications declined 27% versus the same period in 2025 (96,391 cases). Case fatality is 0.06% with 41 confirmed deaths; higher lethality (>0.10%) is seen in La Guajira, Huila, Atlántico and Magdalena. Fifty-three percent of cases (36,997) are concentrated in 35 municipalities. The Orinoquía region is the main epidemiological focus, led by Villavicencio with 8,270 cases. Incidence is highest in those under 17; fatality is highest in those over 65, followed by ages 5–9.

article.articleHeadline: Injectable Bimectin approved in the United States for the prevention of infection in cattle by bloodsucking flies.
article.articleSummary: Emergency-use authorization in the United States for injectable Bimectin (ivermectin-based) to prevent bovine myiasis caused by New World screwworm larvae. Administered by injection during critical windows: within 24 hours of birth, at castration, or after skin wounds. Texas and other states report a rising number of screwworm cases, totaling 47 in the U.S., including three dogs. Bimectin is a generic Ivomec and sold over the counter in injectable form. Restrictions: not for lactating dairy cows; not for calves intended for veal; a 35-day withdrawal period before slaughter to avoid residues. Myiasis can be fatal if untreated, as larvae destroy living tissue. FDA did not fund new safety studies; efficacy is based on 1991–1992 Brazil/Argentina trials showing a single 200 mcg/kg dose prevented myiasis post-birth/castration. Other US-approved options include doramectin and fluralaner (Exzolt Cattle-CA1) — Exzolt requires prescription and is for animals over two months. Veterinary guidance is essential for dosing and prophylaxis.

article.articleHeadline: From Foz do Iguaçu to Cuba: the motorcycle trip that ended in fights, malaria, and repatriation.
article.articleSummary: Expresso Havana documents Ary Neto's motorcycle expedition from Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil to Cuba, undertaken with two university friends on two Suzuki Intruder 125s named Formiga and Pantera, aiming to attend the 8th International Congress of Higher Education in Havana. The journey spans eight countries—Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Panama, and Cuba—traversed amid Pan-American Highway disruptions. Key episodes include mechanical failures, extreme altitudes, and the Darién region crossing between Colombia and Panama, where the trio abandons their bikes due to impassable terrain; malaria is contracted during this segment and diagnosed weeks later in Brazil. After more than two months of strain, interpersonal tensions and route disputes thwart the return by their own means, necessitating repatriation with assistance from the Brazilian Embassy in Havana. The book uses chapter-opening maps to situate readers geographically and emphasizes failure, solidarity, and learning over heroic travel milestones.

article.articleHeadline: Attention! Health department changes rules for yellow fever vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Starting October 1, 2026, Costa Rican citizens and residents traveling to eight countries deemed high risk for yellow fever must receive the yellow fever vaccine at least 10 days before departure and present the International Certificate of Vaccination. The eight destinations are Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, Suriname, Guyana, and French Guiana. The extended deadline does not apply to travel to Colombia, Brazil, and Peru, nor to African risk countries; vaccination remains mandatory for those paths where indicated. The International Certificate of Vaccination can be obtained digitally via the Ministry of Health's Virtual Office, the Unified Health Digital Record (EDUS), and MICITT's Pura Vida Mobile app. This is a preventive measure to mitigate yellow fever importation/exportation with specific digital verification options.

article.articleHeadline: SMS: UEPA Marabá holds first-ever leprosy congress with support from the City Hall.
article.articleSummary: The 1st Amazonian Leprosy Congress took place August 28–30, 2026 in Marabá, Pará, at the Centro de Convenções, organized by UEPA Marabá campus with the Municipal Health Department (SMS). The event gathered professors, researchers, sanitarists, and health professionals to discuss prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of leprosy, aiming to shorten diagnostic delays and interrupt transmission, including pediatric cases. Opening remarks by Marabá Health Secretary Lícia Souza and coordinators emphasized strengthening primary care and ongoing professional training. Organizer Dyana Melkys highlighted expanding regional knowledge and care pathways from diagnosis to hospital care. The program fosters exchanges among health teams and institutions, supported by the UEPA Dermatology and Leprosy Clinic, with patients referred through UBS units. Pará reported about 1,400 leprosy cases in 2025; Marabá currently has 79 patients in municipal treatment. SUS provides free treatment nationwide, with Infectology Society representatives noting continued education and integrated public health action.

article.articleHeadline: Male driver in critical condition due to Whitmore's disease.
article.articleSummary: 54-year-old male driver from Ninh Bình, Vietnam, working at a construction site in Phú Quốc, developed fever with headache, followed by seizures and altered consciousness. Diagnosed with Whitmore (melioidosis) in diabetes. Blood culture grew Burkholderia pseudomallei. On admission to National Institute of Infectious Diseases, he was obtunded with focal seizures; MRI showed thalamic and cortical lesions. He required endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation, with antibiotics and metabolic management. After about a month of treatment, his condition improved substantially, but he must complete the full therapy and maintain glycemic control, with ongoing recovery monitoring. Whitmore is a soil- and water-borne infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, with pneumonia, bacteremia, or CNS involvement. Diabetes increases risk. During the rainy season, avoid mud and dirty water; wear boots and gloves and cover wounds. Seek care if fever, cough, dyspnea, headache, fatigue, or altered consciousness follow soil or water exposure, and inform clinicians of any contact.

article.articleHeadline: Study Maps Hepatitis C Diversity and Drug Resistance Across Viet Nam
article.articleSummary: Vietnam's hepatitis C virus (HCV) epidemic is more diverse than global classifications. A sequencing study of 1,649 HCV genomes from patients sampled 2013–2023 reveals uneven distribution of resistance-associated substitutions (RASs) across genotypes; 37.9% carried RASs, with lineages showing mutations linked to reduced susceptibility to direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) in most samples, while related subtypes remained largely susceptible. Genotype 6 accounted for about half of infections (50.3%), dominated by 6a and 6e, with additional 6h/6l/6o lineages. Genotype 1 was the second most common at 39.4%, with 1a and 1b nearly equal. Genotype 2 comprised 8.5%, genotype 3 1.9%, with regional clustering: 2 in south Mekong Delta and 3 in north. Age patterns: genotype 2 patients were older (median 56) and more often female; genotype 3 were younger (median 36) and predominantly male. HIV co-infection was most frequent with genotype 1; HBV co-infection showed no genotype differences. These findings inform Vietnam's elimination efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases surge in southern Việt Nam, hospitals brace for August-November peak
article.articleSummary: More than 56,000 dengue cases in southern Việt Nam during January-July, with 10 deaths and a 34% rise from the previous year, as vector indicators exceed five-year averages, signaling higher transmission risk. The HCM City Hospital for Tropical Diseases reports over 120 dengue inpatients daily, peaking at about 150. Dengue outbreaks are cyclical; this year mirrors patterns seen in 2022 and 2025, with cycles shortened to three-to-four years. From January 2022 to June 2026, the hospital treated about 105,000 inpatients and 1.9 million outpatients; dengue accounted for 31,098 inpatient treatments, with two-thirds showing warning signs and 17–20% severe. Eight dengue-related deaths (0.03% of treated cases) and 35 severe cases discharged against medical advice were recorded. Preparedness includes a Zalo-based internal reporting system, stockpiles of medicines and diagnostics, ICU capacity, ventilators, dialysis, ECMO and isolation beds, plus data-sharing with Pasteur Institute and HCM City CDC for early warnings.

Authorities continue vaccination campaigns and surveillance, urging reporting of suspected rabid animals to local authorities and veterinary services.

article.articleHeadline: Meningococcal meningitis: A source of transmission that is difficult to detect in the community.
article.articleSummary: Meningococcal meningitis constitutes a hidden community threat, with about 92% of Neisseria meningitidis infections asymptomatic and capable of silent transmission in Vietnam. On 28 August 2026, experts at a Vietnam Medical Association prevention conference urged proactive vaccination to curb spread. Dr. Le Kien Ngai of the National Pediatric Hospital noted transmission via close contact, droplets, and nasal-throat secretions during coughing, sneezing, or talking. Early disease often presents with fever, sore throat, or cough, making detection difficult; once a case is identified, many nearby contacts may already be linked to the source. Recently, cases have been more common in children, not only adolescents. Outbreak risk is hard to gauge because diagnostic testing remains centralized at higher-level facilities. Meningococcemia can progress rapidly, with a 5–15% fatality rate; survivors may suffer neurological, motor, and neuropsychiatric sequelae. Authorities advocate life‑course vaccination and enhanced epidemiological surveillance.

The World Health Organization notes older adults are at high risk for severe complications and death from influenza. The order bans export, import and movement of live pigs and pork products into, within or out of the zones; pork markets and butchery shops within the zones must close. Pig farmers should restrict visitors, disinfect premises daily, and report any unusual illness or mortality among pigs to the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department; suspicious deaths must be reported. Carcasses must be buried per official protocols; dumping in water bodies or open areas is prohibited. Public urged to avoid meat from unknown sources; violators face penalties under the Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act, 2009.

Standing committee chairman Shrinath Bhimale directs priority recruitment and immediate deployment to hotspots, citing delays and urging readiness before the monsoon. A special drive to destroy breeding sites, increase surveillance, and spraying is ordered, alongside regular reviews to ensure manpower reaches high-need areas.

article.articleHeadline: New Dengue Antibody Cuts Viral Load in Indian Phase II Trial
article.articleSummary: Phase II trial of Dengue-mAb, a single-dose monoclonal antibody, conducted at 12 hospitals in India, shows rapid reduction in dengue viremia and faster fever clearance in adults aged 18–60 with fever onset within 48 hours. In 250 randomized participants (249 analyzed), dosing at 3,5,7, or 9 mg/kg IV vs placebo. At 24 hours, adjusted mean log reduction in viremia ranged 0.77–1.21 logs compared with placebo. Among the 32 participants with detectable viremia at baseline, 5,7,9 mg/kg groups cleared viremia by 8 hours, whereas placebo cleared by 72 hours. Fever clearance among baseline febrile patients occurred by median 3.5 hours (5 mg/kg) and 2.0 hours (7 mg/kg) versus 26.8 hours with placebo; 24‑hour fever clearance: 92.9% (3 mg/kg), 100% (5 & 7 mg/kg), 94.1% (9 mg/kg) vs 58.3% placebo. No treatment-related serious adverse events. Phase III planned; results apply to non-severe dengue in adults.

article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-28, H1N1 (swine flu) cases are rising. Although most illnesses are viral, screening for dengue and malaria is underway when fever persists. The spread aligns with rural, monsoon-season infections and reports of vomiting and indigestion tied to contaminated or spoiled food. Rural residents seek care at camps and from informal providers due to information gaps. No specific case or death counts are provided; authorities emphasize dengue/malaria testing where indicated and continued provision of free medicines to curb transmission and manage symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Investigation Bureau busts 71 cross-border smuggling cases / seizes about 1,000 vials of botulinum toxin and 4 tons of animal and plant products.
article.articleSummary: Investigation Bureau, Economic Crime Prevention Division, with Taiwan Customs Administration and the Agricultural and Food Quarantine Service, busted 71 cross-border smuggling cases. The operation also intercepted over 4 tons of meat and fresh fruit, plus large quantities of plant materials and veterinary products. Counterfeit luxury goods were seized, including Chanel, Burberry, and Louis Vuitton items, as well as fake Apple power banks, Bluetooth earphones, and Adidas merchandise. Additional confiscations covered 396 liters of illicit liquor and 10,600 heated tobacco sticks. Wildlife seizures included endangered Indian star tortoise and island bamboo-leaf green snake (Indonesian pit viper) to prevent importation of pests and disease. 71 smuggling cases were investigated.

triage.triage_reason: ボツリヌス毒素の押収は密輸統制・刑事事件であり、感染症の実発生ではない。公衆衛生的な患者・発症事例の報告がなく、IHR基準およびスクリーニング基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本件は密輸摘発・刑事執行事件であり、感染症イベント（患者発生、疾病流行）ではない。ボツリヌス毒素は化学物質/医療材料として押収されたもので、公衆衛生上のアウトブレイク信号ではない。記事サマリーに感染症患者や発症報告はなく、動物・植物のコンタミナントリスク言及も一般的な検疫措置の枠内である。よってシグナルとしてピックアップする価値なし。

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 with a 75% fatality rate, Nipah virus included... Are infectious diseases rearing their heads again—Is Korea safe?
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 cases are rising in China, with July confirmed infections around 522,000, a sixfold rise from June. In Korea, hospitalizations at major facilities increased from 23 (week 30) to 56 (week 33), and outpatient respiratory test positivity rose from 3.2% to 9.1% as surveillance continues after July’s relaxation of the COVID-19 crisis level; the KDCA emphasizes that COVID-19 remains present, with high-risk groups needing vigilance. India reports Nipah virus outbreaks with high fatality; January cases in West Bengal and a June case in Kozhikode, Kerala, led to 104 traced contacts for the Kerala case, with no secondary transmission by June 23. WHO assesses the risk as low; Nipah is a zoonotic virus from fruit bats, transmitted via contaminated foods or fluids, and possible human-to-human spread in care settings. CFR estimates range 40–75%. No wide spread beyond India; no travel restrictions advised.

triage.headline_ja: 致死率75%のCOVID-19、ニパウイルスも…感染症が再び頭をもたげるのか―韓国は安全か
triage.triage_reason: インドで致死率40〜75%とされるニパウイルスの発生が続いており重症度が高く、また中国・韓国でCOVID-19感染者数が急増しメディア・保健当局の関心が高まっているため。
triage.notes: ニパウイルスはインド国内（西ベンガル州・ケララ州）に限定され二次感染も確認されておらず、WHOはリスクを低いと評価。COVID-19は中国・韓国で感染者数増加が見られるが、渡航制限等の措置は取られていない。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1, H3N2 and COVID at once? Why multiple infections are becoming common
article.articleSummary: Reinfection with COVID-19, influenza and H1N1 is possible even after prior exposure, especially for people with comorbidities, undergoing chemotherapy, and pregnant women in India. As of 29 August 2026, experts note antibodies wane over time, and mucosal immunity in the nose and upper airways fades, allowing viruses to re-enter. SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, with new variants enabling immune escape; thus prior infection may not protect against infection with newer strains, though protection against severe disease may remain. Memory B and T cells persist, but antibody levels decrease, particularly in nasal mucosa. Antiviral oseltamivir is most effective when started within 48 hours of symptom onset, underscoring early medical advice for high-risk individuals. The discussion references India-based physicians, including Dr Ishwar Gilada in Mumbai and Dr Bobby Bhalotra at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, highlighting the distinction between infection protection and protection against severe disease, and the role of vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1、H3N2、COVIDの同時感染？複数感染が一般化している理由
triage.triage_reason: 既知の呼吸器感染症（COVID-19、インフルエンザ）の再感染メカニズムに関する一般的な医学解説記事であり、新規アウトブレイクや異常な公衆衛生事象を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は特定のアウトブレイクではなく、免疫学的メカニズム（抗体減衰、粘膜免疫低下）に関する専門家の一般論評であり、具体的な症例数や地域的な感染急増の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: No network, no hospital... the innocent child writhed in pain all night! In Balaghat, 6-year-old Luv Kush dies of malaria.
article.articleSummary: Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh, India, is facing a child-focused outbreak with malaria, measles, and seasonal illnesses. Six-year-old Luv Kush died of malaria on 26 August after Mohanpur Bagatola had no mobile network or nearby hospital. Official records list eight child deaths; the opposition claims up to 25. The family are migrant workers; parents Tulsi Ram Markam and Suklu Markam work in Hyderabad about 700 km away, leaving five children with grandparents. Suklu has four children—Anand, Ankush, Ajay, Luv Kush; Makhan Markam, Tulsi Ram’s brother, has two children: Gagan (1.5) left with grandfather and Radhika (1) taken to Hyderabad. On the fatal night Luv Kush worsened; with no connectivity or hospital access, he died at 4:00 a.m. Burial occurred with family consent to prevent spread; no post-mortem since malaria was suspected. Other affected children were admitted to hospital; former MP Kankar Munjare criticized authorities; tribal groups protest.

triage.headline_ja: ネットワークも病院もない…罪のない子供が一晩中苦しみもがいた！バラガートで6歳のラヴ・クシュがマラリアで死亡
triage.triage_reason: インド・マディヤプラデーシュ州バラガート地区で複数の子供がマラリア・麻疹等により死亡（公式8人、野党主張25人）し、医療アクセス不足や通信網欠如が背景にある。政治的批判や部族団体の抗議など社会的関心も高く、フルリスク評価が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: 発生地はマディヤプラデーシュ州バラガート地区。両親の出稼ぎ先であるハイデラバード（テランガーナ州）は発生地ではなく除外。マラリアと麻疹が同時流行しており、医療インフラ不足が死亡の一因とされる地域限定的な公衆衛生問題。

article.articleHeadline: Health Department falters during Onam season; district-wide communicable-disease prevention efforts off track, five days' data unavailable | news
article.articleSummary: Alappuzha district in Kerala faces faltering Onam-season communicable-disease prevention as health workers take leave, disrupting district-wide surveillance. Five days of vector-borne disease data have not been released; lower-tier facilities struggle to collect reliable information, and available data have not been uploaded online. Only data up to the 23rd of the month have been published; Onam holidays began on the 25th, with the 24th a working day, yet authorities could not gather figures. The report cites widespread circulation of dengue fever, leprosy, H1N1, influenza, and yellow fever-like illnesses, underscoring the need for daily reporting to enable timely interventions. Data collected via IDSP from primary health centers to district hospitals should be transmitted to state and central health ministries, but reporting delays impede rapid outbreak response and containment planning during a critical public-health window.

triage.headline_ja: オナム祭シーズン中に保健局の対応が停滞：県全体の感染症予防対策が軌道を外れ、5日分のデータが未取得
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・H1N1・黄熱病様疾患等複数の感染症の流行に言及しているが、記事の主眼は行政のサーベイランス体制・報告遅延の問題であり、具体的な症例数や深刻度に関する情報が不足している。
triage.notes: 記事はインド・ケララ州アラプーザ県の保健当局によるオナム祭休暇期間中のサーベイランスデータ収集・報告の遅延を主題としている。デング熱、ハンセン病、H1N1、インフルエンザ、黄熱病様疾患の流行が言及されているが、具体的な症例数や発生規模のデータはなく、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Train Food Poisoning: Panic erupts in Mangala Express as 20 children suddenly fall ill one after another; train halted for half an hour at the station.
article.articleSummary: Food poisoning (acute gastroenteritis) incident aboard the Mangala Express saw about 20 children from Kerala fall ill late last night on a Delhi-to-Kerala service. The pantry car meal is suspected as the infection source, with symptoms including vomiting and abdominal pain. At Khandwa railway station in Madhya Pradesh, the train was halted for about 30 minutes as a medical team treated passengers on board. Preliminary medical assessment pointed to food poisoning; no laboratory confirmation is mentioned. After initial care, the train resumed its journey and officials said all children were out of danger. A video circulating shows treatment being administered to some of the children. This event highlights transit food safety risks on long-distance trains; no details of other affected passengers or imported/exported cases were reported.

triage.headline_ja: 列車内食中毒:マンガラ急行で子供20人が次々に体調不良、駅で30分停車
triage.triage_reason: 列車内での食中毒(急性胃腸炎)事案であり、感染症のヒト-ヒト感染や国際的拡大の懸念はなく、原因も食事に特定され対応済みで沈静化している。
triage.notes: 食中毒事案であり感染症の伝播性がないため、EBSシグナルとしての優先度は低い。

article.articleHeadline: African swine fever hits 2 towns in Catanduanes
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) detected in Catanduanes: Virac's Barangay Hicming and Pandan's Barangays Del Sur, Napo, Libod confirmed by RADDL (results released Aug. 27). Eight farmers affected; number of infected pigs pending validation. Governor Patrick Alain T. Azanza ordered immediate isolation of the affected areas and depopulation of infected hogs within five days, with proper disposal. A local ASF task force is to be activated; depopulation within a 500-meter radius of ground zero. Border controls and movement restrictions on live hogs were imposed, with intensified surveillance within a 7-kilometer radius. Police will enforce restrictions. DA Bicol and local governments continue surveillance, including rapid test kits in municipal slaughterhouses to speed detection.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ豚熱、カタンドゥアネス州の2町で発生
triage.triage_reason: 動物疾病(ASF)であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生上の影響がないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに該当性は低い。
triage.notes: アフリカ豚熱は豚のみに感染する動物疾病でヒトへの感染性はない。畜産業への経済的影響及び国内の移動制限措置はあるが、公衆衛生上のシグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: In Kazakhstan, seven imported cases of dengue fever have been recorded since the beginning of 2026.
article.articleSummary: Seven imported dengue fever cases have been recorded in Kazakhstan since the start of 2026, with all infections acquired abroad. Dengue is an acute viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes (Aedes aegypti, A. albopictus) and horseflies; Kazakhstan lacks these mosquitoes, so infection occurs only after visiting tropical or subtropical regions. Affected regions include Southeast Asia (Thailand, Indonesia), Africa, and the Americas (South and Central America). Incubation is 4-10 days post-bite, with symptoms lasting about a week: fever up to 39-40 C, severe headache, retro-orbital/eye pain, myalgia/arthralgia, nausea, vomiting, and rash. Prevention emphasizes air-conditioned, screened housing; long-sleeved clothing; nets for strollers; and repellents applied over sunscreen. Suspected cases should seek medical care promptly; initial care includes high fluid intake and paracetamol, while aspirin or ibuprofen are avoided due to bleeding risk.

triage.headline_ja: カザフスタンで2026年初頭から輸入デング熱症例が7件記録される
triage.triage_reason: カザフスタンにおける輸入症例（海外渡航後感染）のみで、現地でのアウトブレイクや二次感染の報告はなく、対象国での発生でもないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: タイ・インドネシア・アフリカは輸入感染源として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国はカザフスタン（対象国リスト外）。媒介蚊が存在しないため現地感染リスクはなく、一般的な啓発記事に該当する。

article.articleHeadline: Family's hell after gran's rabies death from dog scratch - 'barely broke skin'
article.articleSummary: Yvonne Ford, 59, died on June 11, 2025, four months after a stray Moroccan dog scratched her leg during a February 2025 holiday in Morocco. The very minor wound, cleaned with a wet wipe, was dismissed as insignificant, but the infection progressed, with Ford returning to Barnsley, South Yorkshire. Weeks later she developed a headache, then loss of mobility, confusion, hallucinations, and paralysis; she died in an infectious disease unit after clinicians finally recognized rabies in the context of travel. Her daughter Robyn Thomson warns that ‘tiny scratches’ can be fatal and stresses the need for urgent post-exposure treatment and thorough wound washing. Rabies remains present in more than 150 countries, including Morocco, Turkey, and Thailand. Thomson is partnering with Worldwide Veterinary Service and its Think Rabies Before You Travel campaign to raise awareness and promote pre-travel risk checks and immediate care after exposure.

triage.headline_ja: 家族の悲劇 - 祖母が犬に引っかかれてから狂犬病で死亡「ほとんど皮膚も破れていなかった」
triage.triage_reason: モロッコ渡航中の犬による引っかき傷が原因の輸入狂犬病による死亡例で、既知の感染症による個別症例であり、公衆衛生上の異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は英国在住女性がモロッコ旅行中に犬に引っかかれ狂犬病で死亡した個別症例に関する啓発記事。タイ・トルコは狂犬病流行国の一般的言及のみで、実際の発生国ではない。対象国リストに該当する発生国はなし。

article.articleHeadline: A rare malaria outbreak in Germany: mosquitoes could have arrived by plane.
article.articleSummary: Airport malaria infects six Frankfurt Airport employees in July, Germany, after an initial four cases. The Robert Koch Institute says the most likely source is an infected Anopheles mosquito that could have arrived on a plane, exposing staff after arrival. Plasmodium falciparum, the deadliest malaria parasite, was identified. Early symptoms—fever, chills, and headache—can mimic common illnesses, and lack of recent international travel may delay diagnosis. Blood samples are being analyzed to determine whether a single introduction or multiple introductions occurred. For ordinary passengers, risk remains very low. Frankfurt Airport previously faced similar incidents in 2022, when three staff members contracted malaria without travel; a cargo link from Ghana and the possibility of mosquitoes traveling several kilometers were considered. The report notes climate change and rising imported infections in Europe.

triage.headline_ja: ドイツで稀なマラリア集団発生:蚊が飛行機で運ばれた可能性
triage.triage_reason: 空港マラリアという異常事象だが、発生国であるドイツは対象国リストに含まれず、症例数も少なく重症例・死亡の報告もないため、フルRRAに進める根拠は乏しいが動向は注視が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域はドイツ・フランクフルト空港であり、ガーナは2022年の過去事例における貨物経路の可能性として言及されているのみで、現時点のガーナでの発生ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria at the airport in Frankfurt. The mosquito arrived by plane.
article.articleSummary: Six workers at Frankfurt Airport in Germany contracted malaria, caused by Plasmodium falciparum, with two deaths. Investigations indicate the probable vector was an infected Anopheles mosquito imported by air traffic, leading to airport transmission to employees without travel history to endemic regions. Initial cases rose from four to six; diagnoses were complicated by lack of travel exposure. Blood tests ongoing to determine whether a single mosquito caused all infections or multiple vectors. Germany's Robert Koch Institute notes malaria is rare there; imported/exported cases are a concern for airports. The 2022 Frankfurt incident involved three workers, with genotyping implicating Ghana; Anopheles mosquitoes can travel up to 7 km. Authorities say resident risk is 'very, very low'. Emphasis on rapid antimalarial treatment per WHO and vector control at the airport, staff training.

triage.headline_ja: フランクフルト空港でマラリア発生。蚊が飛行機で運ばれてきた。
triage.triage_reason: 発生国はドイツであり、対象国リスト（ザンビア・フィリピン等）に該当しない。2022年の症例でガーナ由来の遺伝子型が示唆されたのみで、現在ガーナ国内で発生している事象ではないため対象外と判断。
triage.notes: 空港マラリア（airport malaria）事例で、感染はドイツ国内で発生。過去(2022年)の同種事例でガーナ由来の蚊が疑われたことが言及されているが、これは輸入経路の推定であり、ガーナ国内での発生事象ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: A mosquito arrived by plane. Two fatalities at the airport.
article.articleSummary: Six employees at Frankfurt Airport contracted malaria in early July 2026, with two fatalities; none had traveled abroad. All infections were due to Plasmodium falciparum, linked to an infected mosquito believed to have arrived on an aircraft, illustrating airport malaria. The Robert Koch Institute reported cases rose from four to six; diagnosis can be delayed without travel history, risking severe outcomes, while WHO emphasizes rapid treatment. A 2022 Frankfurt cluster of three workers suggested the parasite originated in Ghana; direct mosquito vectors were not identified. Anopheles mosquitoes can travel several kilometers. Experts warn that expanding international travel and climate change increase imported malaria risk in Europe and advocate training for airport and medical staff in recognizing non-endemic diseases. Local authorities say resident risk is currently very, very low; blood analyses monitor whether infections came from a single or multiple mosquitoes, and vector surveillance focuses on the port area.

triage.headline_ja: 空港に蚊が飛行機で運ばれてきた。空港で2人が死亡。
triage.triage_reason: 非流行国のドイツ・フランクフルト空港で「空港マラリア」による死亡例が発生した異常事例だが、対象国（ガーナ）は過去の系統推定として言及されているのみで、現行の発生地ではないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本事例の発生地はドイツ・フランクフルト空港であり対象国リストに含まれない。ガーナは2022年クラスターの寄生虫系統推定として言及されているのみで、現行イベントの発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Why millions of people around the world will contract measles in 2026
article.articleSummary: Measles threatens 11 million infections in 2026, with Africa and Asia bearing most of the burden; outbreaks have also been reported in the Americas and Europe. There is no treatment; vaccines are safe and effective, but herd immunity requires >95% coverage. One-dose protection is good; two doses improve effectiveness. High-income regions approach targets: Europe ~94% one-dose, ~88% two-dose; US >90% of 2-year-olds with at least one dose and >92% of kindergartners with two. In low- and middle-income countries, about 80% receive ≥1 dose and ~70% receive two doses. COVID-era disruptions left many zero-dose children; lab confirmation is rare in LMICs, and counts are underreported, while clinicians note rising cases. In 2026, outbreaks occur in Burundi, DRC, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen; Maldives, Zambia; India experiences surges. Bangladesh reports year's highest measles burden with >900 deaths; vaccine shortages and Gavi funding gaps, amid a mass vaccination campaign in early 2026 vaccinating >1 million children.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年に世界中で数百万人が麻疹に感染する理由
triage.triage_reason: バングラデシュで900人超の死亡が報告されるなど深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、複数地域・複数国（対象国ではインド、ザンビア、コンゴ民主共和国を含む）で流行が拡大しており、IHR基準（深刻な影響・国際的拡大）が2つ以上該当する。
triage.notes: 本記事は2026年の世界的な麻疹流行動向を概説する分析記事であり、特定の単一アウトブレイクの速報ではない。対象国のうちインドでは麻疹の急増、ザンビア・コンゴ民主共和国ではアウトブレイクが報告されているが、詳細な症例数や現地対応状況は不明。バングラデシュ（対象国外）は最大の被害国として言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ワクチン供給不足・Gavi資金不足による国際支援の必要性が示唆される。
